S01.openingCopy: Before you begin, please review how Womb Atlas uses the information you choose to share. Participation is voluntary, and you may pause or withdraw according to the choices explained here.
acknowledgements: I understand the purpose of Womb Atlas.
I understand that participation is voluntary
I understand that Womb Atlas is not a diagnostic or emergency service.
I would like to begin my First Observation
S01.purpose: Obtain informed, understandable, and documented consent before any participant observations are collected.
S01.validation: Mandatory acknowledgement gate; consent version required; timestamp generated; optional preferences stored independently.

adaptive.action: Participant has entered FLOW-1001.
All mandatory acknowledgements are true.
Any mandatory acknowledgement is false or unanswered.
If complete → S02. If incomplete → remain on S01 with clear, non-coercive explanation.
Participant may exit without submitting observations.

S01.aiDisclosure: AI may help organize observations and prepare reflections. It does not diagnose, provide emergency assessment, or make final governance decisions.
S01.qa: No prechecked boxes; cannot proceed without mandatory consent; withdrawal path visible; consent version persisted.
S01.knowledge: KN-1001 Living Observatory Philosophy; KN-1004 Participant Agency Principles
S01.technical: TC-2004 Consent Service; TC-7001 Audit Service

bodyCopy: Womb Atlas observes and helps you understand your health journey. It does not diagnose conditions or replace medical care. Your observations are preserved as an Atlas Record, helping you remember, reflect on, and understand your patterns over time. You can skip any question.
Your answers are organized into an Atlas Record that helps you see your experiences together rather than as isolated symptoms.
After completion, Womb Atlas may provide a reflection that summarizes what you shared, highlights possible patterns, and offers education without diagnosing a condition.
Every observation you share become part of the living observatory, advancing women's health for everyone.
S02.purpose: Explain how participant observations are collected, organized into an Atlas Record, and used to support non-diagnostic reflection.
S02.validation: No required personal data. Completion state saved.

adaptive.action: Valid consent record from S01.
Continue → S03.
If resumed, show only when current orientation version has not been completed or has materially changed.

S02.aiDisclosure: AI may assist with organizing observations and drafting reflections under governed rules. It does not diagnose or replace clinical care.
S02.qa: Consent must precede S02; AI limitation visible; Atlas and Reflection described accurately; back navigation preserves consent.
S02.knowledge: KN-1001 Living Observatory Philosophy; KN-4005 Tracking Your Experiences; KN-6003 Explainability Guidance
S02.reflection: REF-8001 Why This Reflection Was Generated; REF-8002 Understanding AI Assistance
S02.technical: TC-6001 Participant Portal; TC-6002 Mobile Client

S03.openingCopy: This is a quick safety check. Womb Atlas is not an emergency sercive and does not provide a diagnosis.
bodyCopy: Governed urgent safety flags maintained in the Safety Flag Library; exact wording requires clinical approval.
S03.supportCopy: Womb Atlas is not an emergency service. If you believe you are in immediate danger, seek local emergency help.
S03.purpose: Identify participant-reported experiences that may require timely or urgent attention before continuing the First Observation.
S03.inputType: Multi-select safety flags, including a mutually exclusive 'None of these' option.
S03.validation: At least one state selected; mutually exclusive 'None'; safety flag array contains only approved codes.

adaptive.action: If one or more urgent safety flags selected → S04.
If 'None of these' selected → S05.
Continue disabled until at least one response state is selected.
Persist selection locally/server-side according to session policy; re-evaluate route on resume.

S03.aiDisclosure: AI is not used to diagnose emergencies or decide whether you need urgent care.
S03.qa: All urgent flags route to S04; none routes to S05; back navigation retains selections; no diagnostic claims.
S03.knowledge: KN-3001 Care Pathways Overview; KN-3005 Diagnostic Context
S03.reasoning: RC-1005 Observation Quality Assessment; RC-8001 Constitutional Validation
S03.reflection: REF-6001 Preparing for a Healthcare Visit; REF-8004 Confidence and Uncertainty
S03.technical: TC-1002 Collection Service; TC-7001 Audit Service

bodyCopy: You selected one or more experiences that can sometimes need timely medical attention.
Consider contacting an appropriate healthcare service promptly. If symptoms feel severe, rapidly worsening, or immediately dangerous, seek local emergency care.
Womb Atlas cannot assess emergencies or tell you whether a condition is present.
You may continue your First Observation after reviewing this guidance.
S04.purpose: Provide governed, non-diagnostic safety guidance after one or more safety flags are selected.
S04.validation: safety_alert_version persisted when viewed; continue action available.

adaptive.action: One or more governed urgent safety flags selected on S03.
Continue → S05.
The screen provides guidance but does not block completion of the First Observation.
Back → S03, preserving selected flags.

S04.aiDisclosure: This alert is triggered by your selected responses and governed rules, not by AI diagnosis or emergency triage.
S04.qa: Only reachable from urgent S03 route; no diagnosis; no absolute claims; correct local configuration; continuation to S05.
S04.knowledge: KN-3001 Care Pathways Overview; KN-3005 Diagnostic Context; KN-6004 Trust Messages
S04.reflection: REF-6001 Preparing for a Healthcare Visit; REF-8004 Confidence and Uncertainty
S04.technical: TC-6001 Participant Portal; TC-7001 Audit Service; TC-3004 Notification Service where enabled

bodyCopy: Your experiences do not happen in isolation. Age, life stage, hormonal context, pregnancy history, language, culture and access to care may shape how symptoms are experienced and understood.
Context helps Womb Atlas organize observations more accurately and avoid treating every participant as though their circumstances are the same.
S05.purpose: Introduce the Context Chamber and explain why personal, reproductive, hormonal, geographic, cultural and language context helps interpret lived experience.
S05.validation: No required personal data; screen view state only.

adaptive.action: S03 when no urgent flags; S04 after safety guidance.
Continue → S06.
Show when Context Chamber has not been entered for the current First Observation version.

S05.aiDisclosure: AI may later use governed context to organize observations. Context is not used to diagnose.
S05.qa: Reachable from both S03 and S04; copy does not assume cycling, pregnancy, sexual activity or diagnosis; continue routes to S06.
S05.knowledge: KN-4005 Tracking Your Experiences; KN-5001 Observation Definitions
S05.technical: TC-6001 Participant Portal; TC-6002 Mobile Client

S06.supportCopy: Age can shape life stage, healthcare access, and how symptoms are experienced. You may choose 'Prefer not to say.'
S06.purpose: Capture age range as contextual information for interpretation, accessibility, safeguarding, and future longitudinal analysis.
S06.required: Required for current First Observation flow; 'Prefer not to say' is a valid response.
S06.allowedValuesRaw: Under 18; 18–24; 25–34; 35–44; 45–54; 55 or older; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Set adolescent_context = true; apply age-appropriate copy and future assent/consent workflow when enabled.
Continue standard FLOW-1001 route.
Continue → S07.
Age must not be used as a proxy for reproductive state.

S06.aiDisclosure: AI may use the age range only as governed context. It does not determine diagnosis or reproductive life stage.
S06.qa: Prefer-not-to-say permits continuation; under-18 flag is stored; age does not automatically set life stage.
S06.knowledge: KN-4005 Tracking Your Experiences; KN-5001 Observation Definitions
S06.reasoning: RC-1003 Observation Contextualization; RC-4001 Life Stage Interpretation
S06.technical: TC-1002 Collection Service; TC-6001 Participant Portal

S07.participantTitle: Which best describes your current life stage?
bodyCopy: Use 'bleeding' rather than 'period' in canonical wording wherever the meaning is broader than menstruation.
S07.supportCopy: Life stages can change over time. Choose the option that feels closest to your current experience.
S07.purpose: Capture the participant's current reproductive life stage to support adaptive wording and interpretation across later screens.
S07.required: Required; 'I am not sure' and 'Prefer not to say' are valid.
S07.allowedValuesRaw: I have regular bleeding cycles; I have irregular bleeding cycles; I am pregnant; I am postpartum; I am in perimenopause; I am postmenopause; I am not currently cycling for another reason; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: I am not currently cycling for another reason

adaptive.action: Set pregnancy_context = true; adapt wording where clinically relevant; do not assume absence of bleeding or pain.
Set postpartum_context = true; preserve bleeding and pain domains with postpartum-aware wording.
Set menopause_context = true; retain bleeding and pain questions, replacing assumptions about regular cycles.
Set noncycling_context = true; use non-cycling adaptive wording while preserving applicable symptom domains.
Set cycling_context = true; permit cycle-linked wording where appropriate.

adaptive.condition: Not Sure / Prefer Not to Say
adaptive.action: Use neutral wording and avoid routing exclusions.
Continue → S08.

S07.aiDisclosure: AI may use this governed context to organize observations. It does not diagnose pregnancy, menopause, or any condition.
S07.qa: Menopause and non-cycling participants remain eligible for bleeding and pain domains; no screen-skipping based solely on life stage.
S07.knowledge: KN-2007 Hormonal Physiology; KN-4003 Understanding Hormonal Changes; KN-5001 Observation Definitions
S07.reasoning: RC-4001 Life Stage Interpretation; RC-1003 Observation Contextualization
S07.reflection: REF-2002 Symptom Understanding; REF-3001 First Longitudinal Comparison
S07.technical: TC-1002 Collection Service; TC-1003 Collection Flow Service

S08.participantTitle: Are you currently using hormonal contraception?
S08.supportCopy: Hormonal contraception can change bleeding patterns and other body signals. This question does not assume why you use it.
S08.purpose: Capture current or past hormonal contraception use as context for bleeding, pain, hormonal and longitudinal interpretation.
S08.allowedValuesRaw: Yes; No; I have used it in the past but not now; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: I have used it in the past but not now

adaptive.action: Set current_hormonal_context = true; allow future same-screen progressive disclosure for method and duration if governed.
Set past_hormonal_context = true.

adaptive.condition: No / Not Sure / Prefer Not to Say
adaptive.action: Continue with neutral interpretation.
No option removes bleeding, pain, or hormonal questions.
Continue → S09.

S08.aiDisclosure: AI may use this answer as one contextual factor. It does not infer why contraception is used or diagnose a condition.
S08.qa: Past-use option preserved; no downstream symptom exclusion; reason for use is never inferred.
S08.knowledge: KN-2007 Hormonal Physiology; KN-4003 Understanding Hormonal Changes
S08.reasoning: RC-4001 Life Stage Interpretation; RC-5002 Clinical Knowledge Integration
S08.technical: TC-1002 Collection Service; TC-6001 Participant Portal

S09.participantTitle: Your language, culture and location matter
bodyCopy: Language, culture, place and migration can shape how health experiences are described, understood, and supported.
Womb Atlas does not use cultural identity to decide what your body is like or to make deterministic assumptions about risk.
You may select more than one background, use self-description where available, or choose 'Prefer not to say.'
S09.purpose: Introduce why cultural, geographic and language context is collected and establish safeguards against deterministic inference.

adaptive.action: S08 completed or skipped according to configuration.
Continue → S10.
Language preference may alter interface language only after explicit participant selection.

S09.aiDisclosure: AI may use governed cultural and language context to improve communication. It must not infer biology or diagnosis deterministically.
S09.qa: Safeguard language visible; no deterministic claims; route to S10; screen-reader order is logical.
S09.knowledge: KN-1004 Participant Agency Principles; KN-4005 Tracking Your Experiences; KN-5001 Observation Definitions
S09.technical: TC-6001 Participant Portal; TC-6005 Localization Service

S10.participantTitle: Which cultural background or backgrounds best describe you?
S10.supportCopy: These categories may not describe everyone perfectly. Select all that fit, self-describe where available, or choose 'Prefer not to say.'
S10.status: Draft for participant and cultural review
S10.purpose: Capture self-described cultural background as social and contextual information for communication, equity and care-context analysis.
S10.inputType: Multi-select with mutually exclusive 'Prefer not to say.'
S10.validation: Multiple governed values allowed; 'Prefer not to say' is exclusive.
S10.allowedValuesRaw: Black / African / African Diaspora; East Asian; South Asian; Southeast Asian; Middle Eastern / North African; First Nations / Inuit / Métis; White / European; Latin American / Hispanic; Caribbean; Pacific Islander; Mixed background; Another background / self-describe; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Allow multiple backgrounds.
Clear all other selections and self-description.
Show optional text field only when 'Another background / self-describe' selected.
Continue → S11.
Cultural identity may contextualize language, care access and lived experience, but must not deterministically infer biological traits or conditions.

S10.aiDisclosure: AI and reasoning systems must not infer diagnosis, biology or individual risk from cultural identity alone.
S10.qa: Multiple selection works; self-describe field appears conditionally; deterministic-inference prohibition documented; route to S11.
S10.knowledge: KN-1004 Participant Agency Principles; KN-5001 Observation Definitions; KN-9002 Translation Standards
S10.reasoning: RC-4003 Cultural Context Integration; RC-8001 Constitutional Validation
S10.technical: TC-1002 Collection Service; TC-6005 Localization Service

S11.participantTitle: What country do you currently live in?
S11.supportCopy: Your current country helps Womb Atlas understand healthcare and language context. It does not define your identity.
S11.purpose: Capture current country of residence as geographic, regulatory, healthcare-system and care-access context.
S11.allowedValuesRaw: ISO 3166 country list; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: May configure local privacy, consent, support and emergency information.
Must not infer cultural identity or biological risk.

S11.aiDisclosure: Country may be used only as governed geographic context.
S11.qa: Valid ISO values; prefer-not-to-say works; no ethnicity inference; route to S12.

S12.participantTitle: In what country were you born?
S12.supportCopy: This may help describe migration and care continuity. You may choose not to answer.
S12.purpose: Capture birthplace as optional migration and healthcare-continuity context.
S12.allowedValuesRaw: ISO 3166 country list; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: If birth country differs from current country, set migration_context=true without drawing conclusions.
Do not infer migration status, ethnicity or healthcare access automatically.

S12.aiDisclosure: AI must not infer identity or legal status from birthplace.
S12.qa: Optional response; different countries set context flag only; no identity inference.

S13.participantTitle: What language feels most natural when describing your health experiences?
S13.supportCopy: This may differ from the language you use every day.
S13.purpose: Capture preferred language for health expression, translation and communication.
S13.inputType: Searchable language selector with optional self-description
S13.allowedValuesRaw: Governed language list; Another language/self-describe; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Offer participant-approved interface language switch only after explicit confirmation.
Preserve preference for future translation; do not auto-translate sensitive content without governance.
Do not alter reasoning outputs solely because of language choice.

S13.aiDisclosure: AI translation or language assistance must be governed and disclosed; meaning must be preserved.
S13.qa: Preference saves; language switch requires confirmation; free text limit enforced.

S14.participantTitle: Do close family members have a history of any of the following?
S14.supportCopy: Select what you know. It is okay to choose 'I am not sure' or 'Prefer not to say.'
S14.purpose: Capture participant-reported family history as observational context.
S14.validation: Multiple values; None, Not sure and Prefer not to say exclusive according to governed rules
S14.allowedValuesRaw: Fibroids; Endometriosis; PCOS; Heavy bleeding; Infertility/difficulty conceiving; Recurrent pregnancy loss; Early menopause; Cervical cancer; Ovarian cancer; Uterine/endometrial cancer; Another relevant history; I am not sure; None of these; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Store coded contextual observations.
Do not assign diagnosis or certainty; confidence remains participant-reported.

S14.aiDisclosure: AI must not turn family history into a diagnosis or deterministic prediction.
S14.qa: Exclusive options work; multiple conditions persist; no deterministic language.

S15.participantTitle: A few questions about reproductive history
bodyCopy: The next questions ask about reproductive experiences. These experiences are personal, and not every question will apply to everyone.
You may choose 'Prefer not to say' where available. Your answers do not determine your worth, identity or eligibility to continue.
S15.purpose: Prepare participants for sensitive reproductive-history questions, explain relevance and reinforce control.
S15.aiDisclosure: AI may use governed context later but cannot diagnose fertility or reproductive conditions.
S15.qa: Copy is non-coercive; prefer-not-to-say rights are clear; route S16.

S16.participantTitle: Your history may be different from someone else's
bodyCopy: Some people have been pregnant, some have not, and some prefer not to share. The questions that follow will adapt to your answer.
Having never been pregnant will not skip the rest of your health observation.
S16.purpose: Provide a second, brief transition before pregnancy-history questions and clarify applicability.
S16.aiDisclosure: No AI decision is made here; routing follows governed response logic.
S16.qa: Explicitly states that 'No' will not skip all subsequent sections.

S17.status: Draft for scientific and trust review
S17.purpose: Determine whether pregnancy-count questions are applicable while preserving the remainder of reproductive and symptom collection.
S17.required: Required; Prefer not to say valid
S17.allowedValuesRaw: Yes; No; Prefer not to say
S17.criticalRule: No response may skip S19, S20 or later bleeding/pain domains.

adaptive.action: Route → S18 Pregnancy Count.
Skip S18 and route → S19 using not_applicable pregnancy-count state.
Skip S18 and route → S19 without inferring pregnancy history.

S17.aiDisclosure: AI does not infer pregnancy history beyond your response.
S17.qa: Yes→S18; No/Prefer→S19; no route skips remaining First Observation.

S18.participantTitle: How many pregnancies have you had?
S18.purpose: Capture participant-reported pregnancy count when applicable.
S18.allowedValuesRaw: 1; 2; 3; 4 or more; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: S17=Yes only.
All valid values → S19.
Back to S17; changing to No/Prefer clears pregnancy_count according to data-retention policy.

S18.aiDisclosure: Count is contextual and does not produce diagnosis or judgment.
S18.qa: Not reachable after No/Prefer; stale value clears when route changes.

S19.status: Draft for clinical, safeguarding and participant review
S19.purpose: Capture pregnancy-loss history sensitively without excluding participants who answered No or Prefer not to say at S17.
S19.allowedValuesRaw: No; Yes — once; Yes — more than once; Not applicable / I have not been pregnant; Prefer not to say

options.label: Not applicable / I have not been pregnant

adaptive.action: Default applicability display includes 'Not applicable / I have not been pregnant'; do not preselect.
Use neutral wording and retain Prefer not to say.
Route → S20.
Offer pause/skip and support link where governance permits.

S19.aiDisclosure: AI must not infer emotional state, fertility or diagnosis from this response.
S19.qa: All S17 paths reach S19; not-applicable option available; no forced response.

S20.participantTitle: Have you ever tried to become pregnant for 12 months or longer without becoming pregnant?
S20.status: Draft for scientific and participant review
S20.purpose: Capture participant-reported fertility and conception context without assuming pregnancy desire or current goals.
S20.allowedValuesRaw: Yes; No; Not applicable; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Continue → S21 Bleeding Transition.
Do not infer infertility diagnosis, current pregnancy intention, sexual activity or relationship status.
May support optional care-context follow-up without adding mandatory screens.

S20.aiDisclosure: AI must not convert this answer into an infertility diagnosis.
S20.qa: Optional; all values route to S21; no infertility diagnosis language.

bodyCopy: The next questions ask about bleeding you experience now or have experienced recently. This may include regular cycles, irregular bleeding, spotting, postpartum bleeding, bleeding after menopause, or bleeding influenced by treatment.
Choose 'Not applicable,' 'I am not sure,' or 'Prefer not to say' where available.
S21.status: Draft for participant and scientific review
S21.purpose: Introduce bleeding questions using wording applicable to cycling, irregular, postpartum, menopausal and non-cycling participants.

adaptive.action: Use cycle-aware wording without assuming predictability.
Use neutral bleeding wording; do not skip the domain solely because regular cycles are absent.
Allow 'No bleeding / Not applicable' responses and preserve route through impact and progression where historically relevant.

S21.aiDisclosure: AI may organize bleeding observations but does not diagnose causes.
S21.qa: No use of 'period' where broader bleeding meaning is intended; all life stages can proceed.

S22.participantTitle: When bleeding is at its heaviest, how often do you need to change or manage protection?
S22.purpose: Capture bleeding-management frequency as a participant-reported indicator of bleeding burden.
S22.allowedValuesRaw: Every 4–6 hours or less often; Every 2–4 hours; Every 1–2 hours; More than once per hour or leaking through; I do not use products/protection; No bleeding / Not applicable; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: More than once per hour or leaking through

adaptive.action: If participant does not use products, retain response without converting to a low-burden value.
Every 1–2 hours or more frequently contributes to SIG-BLD-001.
When paired with governed dizziness/fainting observations, may surface safety guidance; no diagnosis.

S22.qa: No product-use assumption; not-applicable path valid; threshold signal derived correctly.

S23.participantTitle: How long does a typical bleeding episode last?
S23.purpose: Capture duration of a typical or most relevant bleeding episode.
S23.allowedValuesRaw: Less than 3 days; 3–5 days; 6–8 days; More than 8 days; It varies too much to say; No bleeding / Not applicable; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: It varies too much to say

adaptive.action: More than 8 days → SIG-BLD-002.
'Varies too much to say' is a governed value, not missing data.

S23.qa: Variable and no-bleeding values preserve meaning; signal derives only from explicit >8 days.

S24.participantTitle: Do you notice blood clots when you bleed?
S24.purpose: Capture participant-observed clot presence and approximate size without requiring clinical measurement.
S24.allowedValuesRaw: No clots noticed; Small; Medium; Large; Different sizes; No bleeding / Not applicable; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Large or recurrent different-size pattern may contribute to SIG-BLD-003 under governed rules.
Do not display exact object comparisons unless clinically and culturally approved.

S24.aiDisclosure: AI does not estimate clot size from text or images in the MVP.
S24.qa: No period assumption; not-applicable valid; no diagnostic claim.

S25.participantTitle: Do you bleed at times you do not expect?
S25.purpose: Capture unexpected, inter-episode or unscheduled bleeding across cycling and non-cycling contexts.
S25.allowedValuesRaw: Never; Occasionally; Frequently; My bleeding is too irregular to separate; No bleeding / Not applicable; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: My bleeding is too irregular to separate

adaptive.action: Frequently → SIG-BLD-004.
Use 'unexpected' rather than 'between periods.'

S25.qa: Neutral wording appears for menopause/non-cycling; irregular response is valid rather than treated as missing.

S26.participantTitle: How has your bleeding changed over time?
S26.purpose: Capture participant-reported longitudinal change in bleeding.
S26.allowedValuesRaw: Stayed about the same; Become heavier; Become lighter; Become more frequent; Become less frequent; Become more irregular; Become more predictable; Changed in another way; Not enough history to say; No bleeding / Not applicable; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Heavier, more frequent, or more irregular may contribute to SIG-BLD-005.
At future check-ins, compare governed versions rather than overwrite history.

S26.qa: Historical values preserved; 'not enough history' valid; signal categories map correctly.

S27.participantTitle: How does bleeding affect your daily life?
S27.status: Draft for participant and scientific review
S27.purpose: Capture functional, emotional and practical burden of bleeding.
S27.allowedValuesRaw: Disturbs sleep; Limits leaving home; Requires planning around bleeding; Affects work or school; Affects caregiving; Affects exercise or movement; Causes worry about leaks or access to products; None of these; No bleeding / Not applicable; Prefer not to say

options.label: Causes worry about leaks or access to products

adaptive.action: Any impact except None/Not applicable → SIG-BLD-006.
None and No bleeding are exclusive from impact selections.
Mapped to Function and Daily Life without duplicating participant questions.

S27.qa: Multi-select and exclusivity work; functional mapping generated once; no burden score shown as diagnosis.

bodyCopy: The next questions ask about pain, pressure, aching, cramping or discomfort. These experiences may be constant, occasional, linked to bleeding, or unrelated to a cycle.
If you do not experience pain or discomfort, your path will adapt.
S28.purpose: Introduce pain, pressure, aching, cramping and discomfort in inclusive, non-cycle-dependent language.

adaptive.action: Shown to all life stages.
S29=None routes past detailed pain questions to S35 transition state.

S28.qa: No cycle assumption; pressure/discomfort included; all participants see introduction.

S29.participantTitle: Do you experience pain, pressure or discomfort?
S29.purpose: Establish whether detailed pain questions are applicable.
S29.allowedValuesRaw: Yes, currently; Yes, but not currently; No; I am not sure; Prefer not to say
S29.criticalRule: No pain does not skip later non-pain domains.

adaptive.action: Route → S30.
Skip S30–S34 and route → S35 with no_pain_context=true.
Use neutral route → S30 with optional answers.

S29.qa: No→S35 only; Yes→S30; historical pain retained; no diagnosis.

S30.participantTitle: How often do you experience pain or discomfort?
S30.allowedValuesRaw: Constant or most days; Some days or on and off; During certain phases or activities; Only now and then; Historical but not current; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: Some days or on and off

adaptive.action: Constant or most days → SIG-PAIN-001.

S30.qa: Historical option valid; persistent signal exact; no numeric pain scale.

S31.participantTitle: When does pain or discomfort tend to happen?
S31.allowedValuesRaw: During bleeding; Before bleeding; Around ovulation or mid-cycle; At different times across a cycle; During pregnancy or postpartum; Unrelated to a cycle; Randomly or unpredictably; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: At different times across a cycle

adaptive.action: During/before bleeding or ovulation selections → SIG-PAIN-002.
Hide impossible examples only when clinically justified; always retain unrelated/random options.

S31.qa: Non-cycling participants can answer; cycle options never required; multi-select works.

S32.participantTitle: Where do you feel pain or discomfort?
S32.status: Draft for participant and scientific review
S32.allowedValuesRaw: Pelvis or lower abdomen; Lower back; Legs or hips; Upper abdomen; Bladder or urinary area; Bowel or rectal area; During vaginal penetration or sexual activity; Pain spreads between areas; Somewhere else/self-describe; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

options.label: During vaginal penetration or sexual activity

S32.observationId: OBS-3004 — Pain Location; OBS-3005 — Pain Spread

adaptive.action: Pelvic/lower abdomen/back/legs or spread → SIG-PAIN-003.
Sexual-activity wording includes prefer-not-to-say and does not assume activity.

S32.aiDisclosure: AI must not infer anatomy, diagnosis or sexual activity beyond selected responses.
S32.qa: Body map is optional; all choices have text equivalents; sensitive option is non-assumptive.

S33.participantTitle: What tends to trigger or come with pain or discomfort?
S33.status: Draft for scientific and participant review
S33.allowedValuesRaw: Bleeding; Bowel movements; Urination; Exercise or movement; Sexual activity or penetration; Eating or fullness; Stress or fatigue; Nausea; Bloating; Dizziness; No clear trigger; Another trigger/self-describe; Prefer not to say
S33.observationId: OBS-3006 — Pain Triggers; OBS-3007 — Associated Pain Experiences

adaptive.action: Bowel, urination, movement, sexual activity or bleeding trigger → SIG-PAIN-004.
Stored in the pain profile rather than adding a separate screen.

S33.qa: No-clear-trigger exclusive from explicit triggers; sensitive wording optional; associated symptoms map once.

S34.participantTitle: How do you manage pain, and what does it affect?
S34.inputType: Two grouped multi-select components on one screen

options.label: I do not currently manage it

S34.observationId: OBS-3008 — Pain Management; OBS-3009 — Pain Functional Impact

adaptive.action: Any functional impact except None → SIG-PAIN-005.
No treatment recommendation or effectiveness inference beyond participant response.

S34.qa: Grouped responses remain distinct; no medication advice; none options exclusive within each group.

S35.participantTitle: How has pain or discomfort changed over time?
S35.allowedValuesRaw: Stayed about the same; Gradually worsened; Increased suddenly; Improved; Comes and goes without a clear trend; Not enough history to say; No pain or discomfort; Prefer not to say

options.label: Comes and goes without a clear trend

adaptive.action: When routed from S29=No, preconfigure 'No pain or discomfort' as available but do not silently submit.
Gradually worsened or increased suddenly → SIG-PAIN-006.
Preserve history and compare at check-ins.

S35.qa: No-pain path works; worsening signal exact; no numeric severity scale; routes S36.

S36.participantTitle: Do you experience any of the following pelvic or body-function changes?
S36.status: Draft for scientific and participant review
S36.purpose: Capture urinary, bowel, pressure, abdominal and associated pelvic experiences in one governed screen.
S36.allowedValuesRaw: Frequent urination; Urgency or difficulty holding urine; Pelvic pressure or fullness; Constipation; Diarrhea; Bloating; Abdominal swelling; Pain with bowel movements; Pain with urination; Nausea; Vomiting; Another experience/self-describe; None of these; I am not sure; Prefer not to say

adaptive.action: Two or more urinary/bowel/pressure experiences may contribute to SIG-PEL-001.
Pain-associated selections map to the pain profile without duplicating collection.
None is exclusive from explicit experiences.

S36.aiDisclosure: AI may organize co-occurring experiences but does not identify a condition.
S36.qa: Multi-select persists; none exclusive; duplicate pain mapping avoided.
